character: Unique figure-eight layout, 5.8km. Mix of flowing high-speed sections and technical slow corners. The Esses are the signature — rhythm and commitment define fast laps. Demands a balanced car setup.
sources: https://www.formula1.com/en/racing/2026/japan/circuit official F1 circuit guide; 130R/Spoon/Degner naming well documented

corners.name: First Curve
corners.technique: Light braking or lift, smooth turn-in at 210-230 km/h. Position well for Second Curve
corners.trap: Over-slowing loses momentum through the opening sequence

corners.name: Second Curve
corners.technique: Brake firmly, hit a late apex to open up the entry to the Esses
corners.trap: Early apex compromises the critical S-Curves entry

corners.name: S Curves
corners.technique: Rhythm is everything — light braking or lifts between direction changes, carry maximum speed, trust the car
corners.trap: Over-driving any single apex ruins the whole sequence. Smooth > aggressive here

corners.name: Dunlop Curve
corners.technique: Moderate braking, late apex, good exit feeds Degner approach
corners.trap: Flat-spotting tires under heavy braking on the downhill

corners.name: Degner 1
corners.technique: Quick direction change from Dunlop exit, commit to the speed, clip apex
corners.trap: Hesitation loses huge time; need trust in the car's grip

corners.name: Degner 2
corners.technique: Hard braking, late apex. Exit feeds the straight to the Hairpin
corners.trap: Carrying too much speed from Degner 1 and over-shooting

corners.name: Hairpin
corners.technique: Hard braking, tricky because you're turning while braking. Late apex, patience on throttle
corners.trap: Braking straight is difficult due to approach angle; locking inside front tire

corners.name: Spoon Curve
corners.technique: Late braking into first apex, coast briefly, then smooth throttle for second apex. Exit speed feeds back straight + 130R
corners.trap: Too much speed into first part ruins second apex; poor exit speed loses time through 130R and down the straight

corners.name: 130R
corners.technique: Flat-out in most cars at ~300 km/h. Minimal steering input, trust the aero
corners.trap: Any lift or correction at this speed is enormously costly

corners.name: Casio Triangle
corners.technique: Hard braking from 130R speed, precise through the chicane, clean exit onto start/finish straight
corners.trap: Braking too late after 130R commitment; losing exit speed onto the main straight
